notes:
Here are verse-by-verse notes on 2 John. Every point comes from a page I read, with its address after it. A few gaps first:
- **Lutheran and Orthodox:** I found nothing from lcms.org, 1517.org or oca.org.
- **Pentecostal:** The only source I read from that list was Enduring Word, and it offers no Pentecostal reading of its own.
- **Popular modern teaching:** No page addressed prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace teaching on this chapter. The closest material is the warnings at v. 9 about "new revelation."
- **Partial reading:** The bible.org exegetical commentary cut off partway through its v. 5 notes, so I have nothing from it after that point.
- **Unnamed excerpts:** Several Bible Hub points are excerpts with no commentator's name shown, so I've left them unnamed.

---

**v. 1**
- **The elder.** Enduring Word says Christians have understood from the earliest times that this is the Apostle John. It quotes Clarke: John was about ninety, so "elder" refers to his age rather than to an office. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/
- The Gospel Coalition (TGC, Reformed) instead reads "elder" as a pastoral office title, as Peter uses it in 1 Peter 5:1. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/commentary/2-john/
- **Who is the "chosen lady"? This is the main debate.**
  - *A real woman:*
    - Matthew Henry calls her a person of eminent quality for birth, education, and estate. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/2Jo/2Jo_001.cfm
    - The Pulpit Commentary says a mystical interpretation is not to be resorted to when a plain interpretation is tenable and beautiful. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/homiletics/2_john/1.htm
    - Got Questions sees her as an unnamed friend of John with actual children. https://www.gotquestions.org/elect-lady-2-John.html
  - *A local church:*
    - Enduring Word, quoting Stott, leans this way. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/
    - TGC reads "her children" as the church's members and notes that Scripture often pictures Israel and the Church as a woman or bride. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/commentary/2-john/
    - The bible.org commentary points out that "you" is plural in vv. 6, 8, 10 and 12, which suggests a group. https://bible.org/seriespage/exegetical-commentary-2-john-1-13
  - *A personal name:*
    - The bible.org commentary says "Kyria" as a name was first proposed by Athanasius. It says v. 13 seems to rule out "Electa." https://bible.org/seriespage/exegetical-commentary-2-john-1-13
    - Gill rejects both names and says it can hardly be that two sisters had the same name. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-john/1-1.html
  - *Enduring Word's reason for no names:* John may have left everyone unnamed because of persecution, in case the letter was intercepted. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/
- **Election (Reformed/Baptist emphasis).**
  - Gill says this verse shows election is of particular persons, and not of nations, communities, and churches. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_john/1-1.htm
  - Henry says sometimes election runs in a direct line, meaning an elect lady with elect children. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/2Jo/2Jo_001.cfm
  - The Pulpit Commentary reads "elect" more broadly: chosen out of the world into the Church. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/homiletics/2_john/1.htm
- **"All who know the truth."** Enduring Word says Christians are bound together by shared truth, not by social or political compatibility. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/
- **Catholic view.**
  - The Catholic Encyclopedia lists all the options. It sides with St. Jerome, that the letter is addressed to a particular church, mainly because of v. 13. https://www.newadvent.org/cathen/08435a.htm
  - Catholic Answers calls the lady a symbolic, unidentifiable church under threat. https://www.catholic.com/magazine/print-edition/1-3-john-jude
- **Modern scholarship.** Bible Odyssey suggests the recipient could have been a woman who led a house church and would pass the Elder's concerns to the group meeting in her home. https://www.bibleodyssey.org/articles/second-john-and-women/
- **Less common ideas.**
  - Barclay mentions the suggestion that the lady was Mary, Jesus' mother. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-john/1-12.html
  - Fausset's Bible Dictionary links her to the church at Babylon in 1 Peter 5:13. https://www.studylight.org/dictionaries/eng/fbd/j/john-the-epistles-of.html

**v. 2**
- The bible.org commentary links "the truth that abides in us" to Jesus' promise of the Spirit of truth (John 14:16–17). On this reading the truth is personal, not just doctrine, and stays with believers permanently, as the Spirit does. https://bible.org/seriespage/exegetical-commentary-2-john-1-13
- The Pulpit Commentary says believers hold the truth in their minds, love it in their hearts, and live it out. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/homiletics/2_john/1.htm
- Enduring Word: truth does not change from one generation to the next. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/

**v. 3**
- **"Will be with us."** Enduring Word says John is not just wishing grace, mercy and peace on them but confidently bestowing them. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/ The bible.org commentary reads the future tense as a real promise ("will be"), not a wish ("may it be"), meant to reassure readers facing false teaching. https://bible.org/seriespage/exegetical-commentary-2-john-1-13
- **Mercy.** The Pulpit Commentary: even people who are rich in grace still need forgiveness continually. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/homiletics/2_john/1.htm
- **"Son of the Father."** Enduring Word quotes a commentator who sees an allusion to Christ's miraculous conception, which the Gnostics denied. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/

**v. 4**
- Enduring Word calls John's joy a pastor's heart. Quoting Clarke, it says "children" could mean her own children, church members in her care, or both. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/
- **"Some of your children."** The bible.org commentary says this doesn't necessarily mean others had fallen away. John may simply not have known every member. https://bible.org/seriespage/exegetical-commentary-2-john-1-13
- TGC: obeying God's word is a basic command for every Christian, not an option for the especially committed. What makes us rejoice reveals our hearts. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/commentary/2-john/

**v. 5**
- Enduring Word notes that John pleads rather than commands. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/
- The bible.org commentary says John stresses that the command is "from the beginning" (going back to John 13:34). That sets it against the false teachers' new ideas. https://bible.org/seriespage/exegetical-commentary-2-john-1-13
- *Contending for the Faith* argues that "love one another" is further evidence that the letter is written to a congregation. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ctf/2-john-1.html

**v. 6**
- Enduring Word: love shows itself in obedience. John may have been opposing a vague love with no interest in obeying. It quotes Meyer: They love who obey. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/
- TGC: love is not indulgence. Helping someone do what God forbids is not real love. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/commentary/2-john/

**v. 7**
- Enduring Word says the deceivers held that Jesus only *appeared* to have a real body. It says "coming in the flesh" covers his first coming and also his return in a glorified human body. It also says the spirit of antichrist will be fulfilled in a final, end-times Antichrist. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/
- TGC: they denied the incarnation, a central truth about who Jesus is. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/commentary/2-john/
- **Older critical scholarship.** The 1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica calls the false teachers travelling teachers with "Docetic" views (Jesus only seemed human). It also denies that John son of Zebedee wrote the letter. https://www.studylight.org/encyclopedias/eng/bri/t/the-epistles-of-john.html

**v. 8 — here the traditions really differ**
- **Manuscripts.** Copies differ between "we" and "you" in this verse. The Pulpit Commentary prefers "that *ye* lose not what *we* have wrought," meaning: don't let the apostles' work in you be undone. https://biblehub.com/2_john/1-8.htm
- **Methodist (Wesley).** What is lost is the reward of what they have done, Which every apostate does. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/2-john-1.html
- **Reformed (TGC).** Those who turn away don't lose a salvation they once had. They show they were never truly converted (1 John 2:19). TGC adds that reward is God rewarding deeds fuelled by grace, not something earned. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/commentary/2-john/
- **Barnes.** Genuine Christians can lose *part* of the reward they might have had. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/nas/2-john/1-8.html
- **Bengel, quoted in Jamieson-Fausset-Brown.** There is no half reward of the saints: it is lost entirely or received in full. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_john/1-8.htm
- **Gill.** The reward is not something owed for works. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_john/1-8.htm
- **Bible Hub study notes.** What can be lost is not salvation itself but fruitfulness and reward (1 Corinthians 3:15). https://biblehub.com/2_john/1-8.htm
- **Enduring Word.** Starting well is not enough. We must finish in faith. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/

**v. 9**
- **"Runs ahead."** Vincent says the best manuscripts read "goes onward," meaning going beyond the limits of Christian teaching. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_john/1-9.htm
- One commentator on that page adds that John does not condemn theological progress; he defines its limits. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/2_john/1-9.htm
- Enduring Word quotes Boice: real progress means knowing the biblical Christ more deeply. It quotes Marshall: when the Bible supposedly needs a "key" or a new revelation, that is a sure sign of "advanced" false teaching. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/
- Bible Hub's study notes apply this to teachers who add ideas, practices or revelations that Christ never gave. https://biblehub.com/2_john/1-9.htm
- Barnes: the immediate target is the antichrists of v. 7, but the principle is general. Without true teaching about Christ, no one truly knows God. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/bsb/2-john/1-9.html

**v. 10**
- **Context.** Homes were often where the church met, so welcoming a teacher meant endorsing him. https://biblehub.com/2_john/1-10.htm
- **Ligonier (Reformed).**
  - The teaching in view is the incarnation, but the principle extends to any apostolic doctrine.
  - John is not forbidding contact with unbelievers, or forbidding attempts to persuade false teachers they are wrong. He forbids giving them official approval.
  - https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/do-not-receive-him
- **House or church?**
  - Gill: don't let him preach in the church or stay in your home. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-john/1-10.html
  - Clarke: don't let him preach under your roof. https://www.studylight.org/bible/amp/2-john/1-10.html
  - Enduring Word quotes Stott: the ban may be less about private hospitality than about officially welcoming him into the congregation. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/
- **Limits on the command.**
  - Barnes: be honest and kind to such people as neighbours, but do nothing that supports them as religious teachers. https://www.studylight.org/bible/amp/2-john/1-10.html
  - Henry: they may be helped in urgent need. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-john/1-10.html
  - Enduring Word draws three limits:
    1. The rule covers error that poses as Christianity.
    2. It is aimed at those who *teach* the error, not at those who merely believe it.
    3. It concerns fundamental truths.
  - Enduring Word applies it to groups such as Mormons and Jehovah's Witnesses. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/
  - One excerpt on Bible Hub says John is giving a rule for a special case, not laying down a general principle. It also rejects the medieval idea that promises need not be kept to heretics. https://biblehub.com/2_john/1-10.htm
  - Clarke, quoted by Enduring Word: the apostolic church withheld fellowship and support from false teachers but did not persecute them. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/
- **Early church.** The Catholic Encyclopedia notes that Irenaeus quotes this verse as the words of "John the Disciple of the Lord." https://www.newadvent.org/cathen/08435a.htm

**v. 11**
- Coffman: a greeting signalled the church's approval. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/2-john/1-10.html
- Enduring Word quotes G. Campbell Morgan: these teachers were Gnostics who claimed a deeper knowledge than the simple gospel. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/
- TGC: helping teaching that leads people to destruction is not loving. It applies this to choosing which ministries to support, with giving going first to one's own local church. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/commentary/2-john/

**v. 12**
- The Pulpit Commentary describes the materials: papyrus "paper," ink made of soot and gum, and a reed pen. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/homiletics/2_john/1.htm
- The bible.org commentary says the letter's length fits a single papyrus sheet, about 25 × 20 cm. https://bible.org/seriespage/exegetical-commentary-2-john-1-13
- TGC: the strong warnings come from a loving pastor. Correction works best where love is known, and joy is completed in fellowship. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/commentary/2-john/

**v. 13**
- Enduring Word: most likely a greeting from a "sister" church. It is also a reminder that true believers are more than just our own group. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-john-1/
- The bible.org commentary says people who read the lady as an individual struggle to explain why the sister's children greet her, and not the sister herself. https://bible.org/seriespage/exegetical-commentary-2-john-1-13
- **Reading it as a real family:**
  - Henry sees two elect sisters, probably with elect children. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/2Jo/2Jo_001.cfm
  - The Pulpit Commentary says the sister was not with John. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/homiletics/2_john/1.htm
- **Reading it as a church:** *Contending for the Faith* says the "sister" is the congregation where John worshipped. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ctf/2-john-1.html
